```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

This guide explains the types of objects tidystata returns, how groups and
missing values affect calculations, and how to preview a table without changing
its data. Start with [Getting started](getting-started.html) for a short workflow.

## Container types and lists

```{r containers}
library(tidystata)
library(dplyr)

df <- data.frame(
  group = c("A", "A", "B", NA),
  answer = c("yes", NA, "no", "yes"),
  score = c(2, NA, 6, 8)
)
tbl <- tibble::as_tibble(df)

class(tab(df, answer))
class(tab(tbl, answer))
class(summ(df, score))
class(summ(tbl, score))
```

New tables from the `tab`, `summ`, `codebook` and `variables` families preserve
a base data frame, tibble or data.table input. A list result remains a list, and
each table inside follows the same rule. An explicit output option takes
precedence. `corr()`, `pwcorr()`, `spearman()`, `misstable()` and
`duplicates_report()` are exceptions: they always return tibbles.

Where supported, `.type` selects an output form:

| Value | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `"vector"` | A character vector of names from `ds()`. |
| `"list"` | Separate tables for variables or summary families. `summ()` and `tabstat()` return one table when only one family is present. |
| `"table"` | One table in the input's table class where supported, used by `ds()`, `summ()`, and `tabstat()`. |
| `"auto"` | Retain the input's table class in `fre()`, `tab2()`, and `fre2()`. |
| `"tibble"` | Make each returned table a tibble; combine variable tables in `tab1()` and `fre1()`, or summary families in `summ()` and `tabstat()`. Also supported by `ds()`. |
| `"flextable"` | Format each returned table with the optional flextable package. |

Not every function accepts every value. `tab2()` and `fre2()` still return
lists for multiple pairs or explicit `.by` groups, even with
`.type = "tibble"` or `.type = "flextable"`. `corr()`, `pwcorr()` and `spearman()`
use `.wide` to choose a layout; both layouts return tibbles.

```{r list-and-override}
base_tables <- tab1(df, answer, group)
class(base_tables)
class(base_tables$answer)
class(fre(df, answer, .type = "tibble"))
class(ds(df, .type = "tibble"))
class(summ(df, score, .type = "tibble"))
class(tabstat(df, score, .type = "tibble"))
```

Other data-frame subclasses are not reconstructed on newly shaped tables.
Vectors, such as the result of `ds()` or `row_mean()`, keep their intentional
vector output. New data.table summaries do not retain input keys or indexes.
`as_dummy(.remove = TRUE)` reports an error if its result would be a data.table
with rows but no columns; retain a source or identifier column in that case.

data.table inputs follow the same rule:

```{r data-table}
if (requireNamespace("data.table", quietly = TRUE)) {
  dt <- data.table::as.data.table(df)
  class(tab(dt, answer))
  class(summ(dt, score))
}
```

For a formatted table, install flextable and request `.type = "flextable"`:

```{r rich-output}
if (requireNamespace("flextable", quietly = TRUE)) {
  rich <- fre(tbl, answer, .type = "flextable")
  class(rich)
}
```

## Grouping and denominators

```{r grouping}
grouped <- group_by(tbl, group)
tab(grouped, answer)
summary <- summ(grouped, score, .stat = c("n", "mean", "missing"))
summary
group_vars(summary)
```

Summary and inventory results are ungrouped. Grouping keys remain ordinary
columns where reported. For `tab()`, `tab1()`, `fre()`, `fre1()`, `summ()` and
`tabstat()`, `.by = NULL` inherits existing groups; an explicit `.by` replaces
them. `tab2()` and `fre2()` require explicit `.by` for grouped cross-tabulations;
otherwise, they tabulate the whole input regardless of existing groups.

```{r group-override}
summ(grouped, score, .by = answer, .stat = c("n", "mean"))
```

Cross-tabulation with `tab2()` or `fre2()` returns one table per group, in a
list named after each group:

```{r grouped-cross}
crossed <- tab2(df, answer, score, .by = group)
names(crossed)
```

One-way tabulations use all observations within a group for `percent` and `cum`,
on a zero-to-100 scale. `valid` and `valid_cum` exclude missing measured values.
Missing grouping keys are ordinary groups. In summaries, `valid_pct` is instead
a fraction from zero to one. `summ(.missing = FALSE)` removes missing
grouping keys; numeric calculations always omit missing measured values.

```{r denominators}
tab(tbl, answer)
summ(tbl, score, .stat = c("n", "miss_n", "valid_pct", "mean"))
summ(tbl, score, .by = group, .missing = FALSE, .stat = c("n", "mean"))
```

## Empty and all-missing measurements

```{r empty}
empty <- tbl[0, ]
summ(empty, score, .stat = c("n", "sum", "mean"))
tab1(tbl, starts_with("absent"))

missing <- tibble(a = c(NA_real_, NA_real_), b = c(NA_real_, 4))
summ(missing, a, .stat = c("n", "sum", "mean"))
row_sum(missing)
row_mean(missing)
```

An ungrouped numeric column with no observations remains in a summary with
`n = 0` and `NA` statistics, including `sum`. An all-missing row instead has a
row sum of zero and a row mean of `NA`. Empty selections give empty results for
tabulation; row helpers require at least one column. Matrix columns are not
supported by the tabulation and column-summary interfaces.

## Labels and special missing values

Variable labels describe columns; value labels describe particular values.
Numeric calculations exclude SPSS user-missing codes and Stata tagged missing
values. Tabulations report missing categories alongside observed values.

```{r labels}
labelled <- tibble(
  response = haven::labelled_spss(
    c(1, 2, 99, NA),
    labels = c(Yes = 1, No = 2, Refused = 99),
    na_values = 99,
    label = "Interview response"
  )
)
variables(labelled)
codebook(labelled)
tab(labelled, response)
decode(labelled$response)
```

Summary statistics for labelled numeric measurements use their underlying
values and exclude SPSS user-missing codes. Factors use level codes and warn;
choose measurements deliberately instead of averaging category codes.
`decode()` displays value labels when present, but does not itself recode
every labelled refusal into an ordinary `NA`.

`misstable()` also accepts matrix and nested data-frame columns, using vctrs
missingness for complete rows. Ordinary list columns count scalar `NA` elements
as missing and `NULL` as observed. Structured list-backed matrices instead
follow vctrs cell rules: `NULL` cells are missing and scalar `NA` cells are
observed. See [`misstable()`](../reference/misstable.html) for both output forms.

## Numeric and calendar summary tables

```{r calendar}
mixed <- tibble(score = c(2, 4), day = as.Date("2024-01-01") + c(0, 2))
separate <- summ(mixed, .stat = c("n", "min", "mean", "sd", "max"))
names(separate)
separate$numeric
separate$date
class(separate$date$sd)
combined <- summ(mixed, .type = "table", .stat = c("n", "min", "mean", "sd", "max"))
combined
class(combined$sd)
```

Default list mode keeps numeric statistics numeric in their own table. Calendar
locations such as `min`, `mean` and `max` are formatted dates or date-times,
while a spread such as `sd` stays a `difftime`. Table mode combines families.
A location column shared by numeric and calendar rows becomes character, and the
spread column becomes a plain number of days for dates or seconds for
date-times, with the unit shown in the `type` column.

SD uses the sample denominator. Percentiles use Stata's rule; for example,
the quartiles of `1:4` are 1.5 and 3.5. See
[`summ()`](../reference/summ.html) for formulas, weights and other statistics.

## A preview retains every row

```{r previews}
long <- tibble(id = 1:12, value = (1:12)^2)
view <- preview_headtail(long, n = 4)
view
nrow(view)
sum(view$value)
```

The preview still contains all 12 rows. `n` is the total display budget,
split between the beginning and end. A single row of dots marks an omitted
middle. Interval previews show approximately evenly spaced positions without
separator rows; sort first when position should represent a meaningful order.
Both styles report how many rows are omitted from the display.

```{r remove-preview}
preview_interval(long, n = 4)
ordinary <- unpreview(view)
identical(ordinary, long)
```

`print_headtail()` and `print_interval()` print once and invisibly return the
complete input. `unpreview()` removes the persistent display setting.
Supported dplyr/tidyr operations carry preview settings forward while following
their own container and grouping rules. Wrapping and unwrapping a data.table
copies it; later native data.table mutations retain ordinary reference semantics.
